$comment: Findings that describe how CI runs Bowire rather than what Bowire is (#614).
Scanning our own instance is only worth doing if the alerts that come out
are ones Bowire can actually fix. A workflow that starts the tool on
http://localhost and uploads 'target serves plaintext http://' has not
found anything about the product — it has described its own scaffolding,
and an operator reading the Security tab concludes Bowire ships without
TLS. That is the mistake scan-dogfood.yml refuses to make by not
uploading at all; here we do want the upload, so an exclusion has to be
explicit and named instead.
The bar for adding a rule here: would this finding disappear if the same
build ran behind a load balancer with a certificate? If yes it is the
harness's. If it would still be true of a correctly deployed Bowire, it
stays and gets fixed.
The list is EMPTY, and that is the goal rather than an oversight. It held
exactly one entry, BWR-BUILTIN-TLS-001, because the scan ran over
plaintext. #634 made Bowire honour ASPNETCORE_URLS and Kestrel:Endpoints
instead of overriding them, so the scan now runs over TLS with a
certificate the job issues itself — the finding is gone because the cause
is gone, which is a better outcome than an exclusion that hid it. It also
unblocked BWR-REST-001: Strict-Transport-Security is only sent over TLS
(RFC 6797 §8.1), so over http:// that rule could never be closed honestly.
Deliberately NOT excluded: BWR-BUILTIN-BANNER-SERVER. `Server: Kestrel`
was emitted because Bowire did not set AddServerHeader = false, and that
was true of every deployment, behind any ingress. It was ours, and #625
fixed it rather than excluding it.
Prefer fixing the harness over adding a rule. Every entry here is a
finding nobody will see again.
